---
title: "Styles"
---

Styles are defined once in a palette and referenced by ID.

## The palette

```json
{
  "styles": {
    "defs": { "header_bold": { "font_weight": "bold" } },
    "compositions": { "header_right": { "extends": "header_bold", "overrides": { "text_align": "right" } } },
    "conditionals": [{ "id": "stripe", "selector": { "row_parity": "even" }, "style": { "background_color": "#FAFAFA" } }]
  }
}
```

<!-- ir-fields: StylePalette -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `defs` | map of StyleDef | `{}` | Style definitions, by style id |
| `compositions` | map of StyleComposition | `{}` | Compositions, by style id ([below](#compositions)) |
| `conditionals` | array of ConditionalStyle | `[]` | Styles for the rows a selector matches ([below](#conditional-styles)) |

A style id is a key of `defs` or `compositions`.

## Style Definition Fields

All fields are optional; specify only what you need. Keyword fields accept the values
listed in [Keyword values](validation.qmd#keyword-values), lengths the forms in
[Lengths](validation.qmd#lengths) and colors those in [Colors](validation.qmd#colors);
anything else fails validation.

<!-- ir-fields: StyleDef -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `font_family` | string? | `null` | CSS font list (`"Georgia, serif"`) |
| `font_size` | length? | `null` | A length or a CSS size keyword (`small`, `larger`, …) |
| `font_weight` | keyword or number? | `null` | `"normal"`, `"bold"`, `"bolder"`, `"lighter"`, or 1–1000 (string or number) |
| `font_style` | keyword? | `null` | `"normal"`, `"italic"`, `"oblique"` |
| `color` | color? | `null` | Text color |
| `background_color` | color? | `null` | Background color |
| `text_align` | keyword? | `null` | `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`, `"justify"`, `"char"` |
| `vertical_align` | keyword? | `null` | `"top"`, `"middle"`, `"bottom"`, `"baseline"`, `"super"`, `"sub"` |
| `text_transform` | keyword? | `null` | `"none"`, `"uppercase"`, `"lowercase"`, `"capitalize"` |
| `text_decoration` | keyword? | `null` | `"none"`, `"underline"`, `"overline"`, `"line-through"` |
| `white_space` | keyword? | `null` | `"normal"`, `"nowrap"`, `"pre"`, `"pre-wrap"`, `"pre-line"`, `"break-spaces"` |
| `padding` | Padding? | `null` | Space inside the cell, by side ([below](#padding)) |
| `border` | BorderSet? | `null` | The cell's borders, by side ([below](#borders)) |
| `indent` | length? | `null` | Indent of the first line (may be negative) |
| `word_break` | keyword? | `null` | `"normal"`, `"break-all"`, `"keep-all"`, `"break-word"` |
| `overflow` | keyword? | `null` | `"visible"`, `"hidden"`, `"clip"`, `"scroll"`, `"auto"` |
| `text_overflow` | keyword? | `null` | `"clip"`, `"ellipsis"` |
| `min_width` | length? | `null` | The least the cell is wide |
| `max_width` | length? | `null` | The most the cell is wide |

What each format does with each property is in the
[Feature Matrix](../guide/feature-matrix.qmd).

Outside HTML, `"baseline"`, `"super"` and `"sub"` place a cell's content at the top:
in a table cell they line up the first lines of a row's cells, which is where top
alignment puts them when the cells share a font size. LaTeX output doesn't write
`vertical_align` (see the [Feature Matrix](../guide/feature-matrix.qmd)).

How formats other than HTML write `font_family` and `text_transform` is described in
[Output Formats](../guide/output-formats.qmd).

### Padding

<!-- ir-fields: Padding -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `top` | length? | `null` | Padding above the content |
| `right` | length? | `null` | Padding to its right |
| `bottom` | length? | `null` | Padding below it |
| `left` | length? | `null` | Padding to its left |

### Borders

<!-- ir-fields: BorderSet -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `top` | Border? | `null` | The top border |
| `right` | Border? | `null` | The right border |
| `bottom` | Border? | `null` | The bottom border |
| `left` | Border? | `null` | The left border |

Each side is a border:

<!-- ir-fields: Border -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `width` | length? | `null` | Border width (`"1px"`) |
| `style` | keyword? | `null` | `"none"`, `"hidden"`, `"solid"`, `"dashed"`, `"dotted"`, `"double"` |
| `color` | color? | `null` | Border color |

## Example

```json
{
  "styles": {
    "defs": {
      "header_bold": {
        "font_weight": "bold",
        "background_color": "#f0f0f0",
        "border": {
          "bottom": { "width": "2px", "style": "solid", "color": "#333333" }
        }
      },
      "numeric": {
        "font_family": "Courier New, monospace",
        "text_align": "right"
      }
    },
    "compositions": {
      "header_numeric": {
        "extends": "header_bold",
        "overrides": { "text_align": "right" }
      }
    },
    "conditionals": [{
      "id": "stripe",
      "selector": { "row_parity": "even", "scope": "tbody" },
      "style": { "background_color": "#FAFAFA" }
    }]
  }
}
```

## How Styles Combine

Every writer resolves a cell's style the same way (in `gridwell-layout`). The layers,
lowest to highest priority:

1. the column's default style (`column_spec[].style_id`), for body and summary cells
   (column labels are styled by their own row and cell styles);
2. row striping (`config.row_striping`, see [Config](config.qmd#row-striping));
3. each matching conditional style, in the order listed (later ones win);
4. the row's style (`row.style_id`);
5. the cell's style (`cell.style_id`).

A layer overrides only the properties it sets; everything else shows through from the
layers below. `padding` and `border` merge side by side, so a cell style that sets only
`border.bottom` keeps a row style's `border.top`. A border edge whose style is `none`
or `hidden` removes that edge. Values that don't parse (and keywords outside their
allowed set) are ignored, so they never reach any output.

A style id is a non-empty name of ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-` (anything else
fails validation with `INVALID_STYLE_ID`): writers put ids into markup, such as HTML
class names. A style id can name a definition or a composition, but not both
(`DUPLICATE_ID`).

### Compositions

A composition is its `extends` definition with `overrides` laid over it;
compositions don't chain.

<!-- ir-fields: StyleComposition -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `extends` | string | required | The id of the definition (in `defs`, not a composition) it starts from (`STYLE_REFS_VALID` otherwise) |
| `overrides` | StyleDef | `{}` | The properties it sets in place of the definition's |

### Conditional styles

<!-- ir-fields: ConditionalStyle -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | required | The conditional style's id |
| `selector` | ConditionalSelector | required | The rows it applies to (`{}` for every row) |
| `style` | StyleDef | required | The properties it sets on their cells |

<!-- ir-fields: ConditionalSelector -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `row_parity` | keyword? | `null` | `"odd"` or `"even"`: every other row ([below](#conditional-selectors)) |
| `scope` | keyword? | `null` | `"tbody"`, `"thead"` or `"table"`: the rows it applies to |

### Conditional selectors

| Selector field | Values | Matches |
|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `tbody` (`body`) | data rows of every group (not summary rows) |
| | `thead` (`head`) | column-label rows |
| | `table` (`all`), or absent | every row |
| `row_parity` | `odd`, `even` | rows numbered from 1, as in CSS `:nth-child(odd)`: data rows count across all groups, head rows within the head, summary rows within their group |
| | absent | every row in scope |

Unknown values match nothing (and are reported as `UNKNOWN_VALUE`).

## Color Values

- Named: all 148 CSS named colors (`red`, `steelblue`, `rebeccapurple`, …)
- Hex: `#RGB`, `#RGBA`, `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`
- Functional: `rgb()`/`rgba()` and `hsl()`/`hsla()`, in comma syntax
  (`rgb(255, 0, 0)`) or space syntax with optional alpha (`rgb(255 0 0 / 50%)`)
- Keyword: `transparent`

Anything else fails validation with `INVALID_COLOR`; see
[Validation](validation.qmd#colors) for details and for the length forms each field
accepts.
